title: Live imaging of postembryonic developmental processes in C. elegans
protocol: Prepare 10% (w/v) agarose solution by boiling 2 g agarose in 20 mL M9 buffer.
Aliquot 5 mL of the prepared agarose solution into a 15 mL centrifuge tube and keep it on a thermostatic Dry Bath at 80°C to maintain as liquid state.
Store the aliquoted agarose solution at 4°C for up to 2 months.
When needed, place the stored tube in water and heat it in a microwave oven carefully to avoid boiling over.
Place the heated agarose solution in a Dry Bath to keep it molten.
Prepare two glass slides by pasting a layer of paper tape on both sides of each slide.
Put the prepared glass slides parallel on a table with a clean glass slide in between.
Drop 10% melted agarose onto the middle glass slide.
Gently place another glass slide across the three slides to form an agarose pad.
Place Vaseline and Paraffin in a thermostatic Dry Bath at 80°C to melt them.
Mix melted Vaseline and Paraffin at a 1:1 volume ratio.
Seal the gap between the glass slide and the coverslip with the mixed Vaseline and Paraffin solution.
Add more mixture of Vaseline and Paraffin to areas that are not completely sealed.
Use another glass slide to slowly scrape protruding white wax until the thickness is uniform.
Place 50–100 μL of 10% molten agarose onto the center of the middle slide.
Immediately place another slide across the three slides to form an agarose sandwich.
Wait about 1 minute for the agarose to solidify, then gently remove the top slide.
Place the middle slide with the solidified agarose pad in a humidity chamber.
Place 10–20 synchronized larval C. elegans into the 2.5 mM levamisole solution on the pad using a worm picker.
Wait until the movement of the larvae becomes not obvious.
Put the coverslip onto the pad containing the immobilized larvae.
Wash worms with M9 buffer in a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Spin the tube in a tabletop centrifuge at 1,000 × g for 15 s.
Aspirate to 100 μL and add 100 μL of 5 mM levamisole.
Transfer worms (25–50 μL) using a Pasteur pipet to the agarose pad.
Absorb excess liquid with filter paper.
Wait for 30 s before placing the coverslip on the pad.
Make a 1:1 mixture of Paraffin and Vaseline.
Apply the mixture along the edge of the coverslip to seal the gap between the coverslip and the slide.
Use Nikon Spinning Disk confocal microscope with an air lens 10×/ 0.5 N.A objective for finding worms and an oil lens 60×/1.4 N.A objective for high-resolution imaging.
Image with a spinning disk confocal scanner unit CSU-W1 using NIS-Elements AR 5.20.00 software.
Capture images with a Photometrics Prime 95B camera.
Set the parameters of CSU-W1 to 4,000 rpm disk-spin speed, pinhole 50 μm and use a 561 nm excitation laser wavelength at 10% power with an exposure time of 200 ms.
Set the room temperature between 20°C and 25°C for imaging.
Place the slide on the inverted fluorescence microscope stage.
Find worms under air lens 10×/ 0.5 N.A objective using the automated stage of acquisition software.
Mark the location of worms with the automated stage.
Select healthy L1 larvae under a higher-magnification 60× objective.
Examine the development stage of Q cells.
Choose the stage before the first division and mark its position.
Acquire a stack of mCherry images with 18 planes at 1 μm intervals every 10 minutes using an automated stage for multiple positions.
Select worms with minimal curling to image.
Avoid selecting worms that are close to each other to ensure imaging quality.
Set up acquisition parameters for imaging.
Use an excitation laser wavelength at 561 nm.
Set the laser power to 10%.
Set the exposure time to 200 ms.
Configure Z stack intervals at 1 μm.
Set a frame rate of 10 minutes.
Create a new data folder.
Set parameters for automatically saving live-imaging data.
Reduce photodamage by setting longer frame intervals and fewer Z stacks if needed.
For studying asymmetric cell division within 1 hour, set time intervals to 30–60 seconds.
To examine cell migration and apoptosis over more than 3 hours, set time intervals at 5–10 minutes.
Track Q cell lineage development taking approximately 10 hours.
Limit live imaging duration to no more than 4 hours for physiological activity and high-quality images.
Place the prepared slide on the stage of an inverted fluorescence microscope.
Find worms under air lens 10×/ 0.5 N.A objective and mark their location.
Select healthy L2 larvae with proper straight body and without other worms nearby for imaging.
Examine the development stage of PVD dendritic at 20× objective.
Switch to a higher-magnification 60× objective for detailed observation.
Set up image parameters: laser scan confocal PMT (HV 86), 20.4 μm pinhole size, one way scan direction, 2.288× zoom, laser scan speed at 0.25 fps, laser wavelength at 488 nm, 5% laser Power.
Capture Z-stack images at 0.5 μm intervals with a 10 min time interval for a 3.5 h duration.
Set the time interval to 30 s–60 s within 1 h for detailed observation of dendrite branching and self-avoidance.
Minimize laser power and exposure time to reduce phototoxicity.
Find other worms or make a new slide if PVD dendrites stop growing for more than 30 min.
